note: A multi-bit internal combinational wire as a fault site. The corpus injects into internal signals already, but only narrow ones arriving by other routes - struct_mux's nsel is one bit out of a gate primitive, hier_adder's s1 one bit left by an inlined instance, pipeline3's s1 a register whose effect lands cycles later. sel here is an ordinary eight-bit wire written by a continuous assignment, reaching y in the same delta. Because the second statement inverts, the same fault type at the two locations drives the output opposite ways: forcing sel[3] high drives y[3] low, forcing y[3] high drives it high. The two oracles therefore move disjoint rows, which is what shows the locations are different points in the dataflow rather than one point named twice - an instrumentation that collapsed the intermediate would make both faults agree, in valid RTL.
